privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: ListenLoop is an English listening practice site. This policy explains what data we collect, how we use it, where it's kept, and how you can delete it. Every practice feature works without signing in.

sections.title: What we collect
paragraphs: Only when you sign in (Google, LINE, or email) do we collect the following:
items: Account details from how you sign in: from Google, your email, name, picture URL, and account ID; from LINE, your email, display name, and LINE user ID; with email sign-up, your email and password. Supabase stores the password hashed, so we never see it. Only the email is shown on screen.
One account: whichever way you sign in, one email is one account, and your progress is combined.
Practice data: your progress on each video (which days are done, dictation answers and accuracy, shadowing status) and a daily practice log.

Created practices: the text you type or upload when creating a practice, its sentences and translations, the vocabulary and grammar notes, and the generated audio; for a practice from your own recording, the recording you upload (your browser first turns it into a smaller MP3; for a video, only the sound is uploaded, never the picture).

Sharing and reports: anyone can see a public practice's title, sentences, translations, notes, and audio, but not its author's account details. When you report a practice, we keep the reason, your details, and your account ID only to review it; the author isn't told who reported it.
Sign-in state: a sign-in token in a browser cookie.

Account data: the user number the system gives you, your role (user or admin), account status, and when you joined and were last active. The admin pages identify users by number and don’t show emails.

Activity log: events such as signing in, starting a practice, completing a day (with its score), retrying, creating, editing, deleting, or publishing a practice, reporting, skipping a sentence, speech recognition failures, and deleting your account. Only your user number and the needed fields (practice code, day, score, a short code) are kept — never practice text, recognized speech, or recordings.

Hard-sentence reports: when shadowing one sentence stays under half five times in a row and you choose “Try again” or “Skip and report,” we keep the sentence’s position, each try’s coverage, the text speech recognition heard, your browser and system names, and whether you skipped; and, if you’re signed in, your account. Text only, never audio. You can report without signing in, in which case no account is kept.
Feedback: what you send us, and (if signed in) your account.

Practice reminders (optional): if you turn on reminders on the account page, we keep the push subscription your browser provides (the push service address and encryption keys) and the time you chose, to send one reminder a day; turning reminders off deletes it.
Satisfaction survey: if you answer the survey after Day 7, we keep the score (0–10), your optional comment, the material's code, and the week.

Referrals: when you sign up through a friend's link, we record who invited whom, when, whether Day 1 was finished, and the minutes each side got; to tell whether both are the same person we compare the sign-up IP hashes and the practice device codes, and never show these to the other person. A referrer sees only counts, not the accounts they brought.
Abuse prevention: sign-up and some actions record a hash of the connection's IP address (it can't be turned back into the IP) to limit bursts of requests and spot many sign-ups from one source.

Interest in paying and price tests: your steps on the pricing page and upgrade prompts (viewed, switched monthly or yearly, pressed subscribe, joined the waiting list), and which price-test group you're in. The same account (or browser) always sees the same test price. When you join the waiting list, we note the plan, period, and price you saw, so the early-bird offer can use that price when paying opens.
Price survey (optional): if you answer the 4 price questions after Day 7 or a while on the pricing page, we keep the 4 amounts and where you answered (Day 7 or the pricing page).

sections.title: When you're not signed in
paragraphs: Your progress stays in your browser (localStorage) and is never sent to our servers. The interface language is kept in a cookie and the theme in localStorage. Clearing your browser data removes them.

When you open the pricing page, your browser keeps a random visitor id (a cookie, for 180 days) so a price test shows you the same price each time and interest can be counted; it isn't linked to anything personal. A price survey answered while signed out is kept only under this id.

sections.title: How we use it
paragraphs: We use this data to sign you in and keep your progress in sync across devices; to provide features such as creating materials, AI notes, and audio; to prevent abuse and keep the service secure (for example rate limits and bot checks); and to improve the product from feedback, surveys, and the anonymous activity log.
We don't sell data, share it with advertisers, or use advertising trackers; usage analytics run only if you agree (see "Usage analytics"). We don't send marketing email.

sections.title: Where it's kept and who processes it
items: Supabase: the database for accounts and cloud practice data, in the United States (us-east-1). Recordings you upload are kept in Supabase's private storage and can only be read through links that expire.
Vercel: the web host, which handles the technical data a connection needs (such as IP addresses) to serve and protect the site.
Google: Google sign-in.

Microsoft Azure AI services: when you create a practice, its text is sent to Azure OpenAI (the gpt-5-mini model) to split it into sentences, translate it, and write vocabulary and grammar notes, or to write practice text for the situation you pick; its English sentences go to Azure Speech for audio; for a practice from your own recording, the recording is sent in short pieces to Azure Speech's speech to text, which writes it down with each sentence's times. Under Microsoft's terms, what's sent and what's generated aren't used to train models. Azure OpenAI may keep them for up to 30 days to detect abuse, and may process them in any of Microsoft's regions (a Global Standard deployment); Azure Speech processes them in the United Arab Emirates. Even so, please don't put personal or sensitive information in practice text.
YouTube: built-in video materials (such as the Blender open movies) play through YouTube (youtube-nocookie.com); once a video plays, YouTube may set cookies under Google's privacy policy.

Speech recognition: shadowing uses your browser's built-in speech recognition; in Chrome, audio is sent to Google's servers to be recognized. ListenLoop doesn't record or store audio, only whether each sentence is done and how much was heard.
LINE (LY Corporation): when you sign in with LINE, it handles the sign-in and gives us your account details.

Cloudflare Turnstile (when turned on): the sign-up, waiting list, report, and feedback forms use it to tell people from bots; it handles technical data about the browser and connection, not for advertising.
Push services: when practice reminders are on, they reach you through your browser maker's push service (for example Google, Apple, or Mozilla).
GitHub: the database's daily backups are encrypted (AES-256) and kept in GitHub Actions for 14 days; they can't be read without the password.

sections.title: Your writing
paragraphs: In Writing (WritingLoop), your essays, drafts, AI feedback, notebook, and own prompts stay in this browser when you're signed out; signed in, they're also kept in your account where only you can see them (the database lets only you read or write them). Admin pages show usage counts only, never what you wrote.

For AI feedback, your essay is sent to an AI service (Azure OpenAI) to be scored; our server doesn't keep a copy. We never use your writing to train AI models, and under Azure OpenAI's terms what is sent isn't used for training either.

Chat practice: each message is sent with the recent conversation to an AI service (Azure OpenAI) for the reply and tips; our server doesn't keep the conversation. It stays in this browser and your account, only for you, and you can delete it under Past chats. The server records only each chat's start time, length, and number of messages, for the weekly chat messages. Reporting a reply sends only that AI reply and the situation to the admins, never your messages.

Extra practice's AI check: answers that differ from the sentence are sent with the sentence to an AI service (Azure OpenAI) at the end of a set, to judge their meaning and grammar; the server doesn't keep them, and the results stay in this browser and your account. You can turn it off in your writing settings.

Back-translation audio: model sentences and your own corrected sentences are voiced by a speech service (Azure Speech) and kept in the shared speech cache, named by a hash of the sentence, with nothing about your account; only someone who knows the whole sentence can find it. Your own sentences are voiced only when you're signed in, counted against your daily speech allowance.
How long: essays and feedback are kept until you delete them. Deleting your account deletes them; signed out, clearing the browser's data does.

sections.title: Usage analytics (Microsoft Clarity)
paragraphs: Only after you choose "Accept analytics cookies" do we load Microsoft Clarity, which records anonymously how the site is used, so we can find what's hard to use and improve it. Without your consent, or when the site hasn't set Clarity up, it isn't loaded at all.
items: What's recorded: clicks, scrolling, pointer movement, and changes on the page (replayed as recordings and heatmaps), browser and device type, and approximate location (country).

Masking: everything typed into inputs is masked and never recorded; the email in the account menu is masked; the account, sign-in, class, and admin pages are masked whole. We don't link recordings to your account.
Cookies: Clarity keeps analytics cookies in your browser (such as _clck and _clsk) to connect the pages of one visit. We set Clarity to analytics only, not advertising.
Processor: Microsoft Clarity is provided by Microsoft; data may be stored in the United States and is handled under Microsoft's privacy statement (https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement).
Change it any time: "Cookie settings" at the bottom of the page switches to "Necessary cookies only", and Clarity isn't loaded after that; you can also clear your browser's cookies.

sections.title: Payment data
paragraphs: When you subscribe to the paid plan, payments are handled by a third-party payment service (not open yet). It collects and keeps your card and payment details; ListenLoop never sees or stores your full card number.

We keep only what the subscription needs: the plan, billing period, next payment date, and each payment's amount, currency, date, and status (paid or refunded), to provide the paid features, show your payment history, handle refunds, and keep transaction records as the law requires. Deleting your account deletes these too, except records the law requires us to keep.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: Your account and practice data are kept while your account exists. The activity log is kept 180 days and hard-sentence reports 365 days, then deleted automatically. The API usage log (number of calls, tokens, characters, estimated cost — no text) is kept to account for service costs; deleting your account removes its link to you. When you delete your account, your account, practices, activity, reports, and feedback are deleted from the database right away; audio files of your practices are deleted too, unless another practice shares them; recordings you uploaded are deleted with their practice or your account. Service providers’ system backups are cleared when their retention ends.

Other records are kept for: error logs 90 days, abuse-prevention IP hashes 90 days, rate-limit counters 1 day, encrypted backups 14 days; survey answers while your account exists, deleted with it. Interest records are kept for 365 days; price survey answers while your account exists, and deleted with it.

sections.title: Your choices and rights
items: You can sign out at any time; your practice data stays on this device.
On the Account page you can download your data (JSON): your account data, cloud progress, the practices you made, your activity, reports, and feedback.
On the Account page you can permanently delete your account and cloud data, which also clears the practice data on this device.
To see, correct, or delete your data, or with any other privacy question, contact us through “Feedback” at the bottom of the page.

sections.title: Young users
paragraphs: ListenLoop is mainly for high school and university students. If you’re under 18, use it with the consent of a parent or guardian who has read this policy. If you’re under 13, don’t create an account yourself. When you create a practice of your own, the text you type or upload is sent to AI services to be processed (see above), so don’t include personal information.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: When this policy changes, we update this page and the date above. Major changes are also announced on the site.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: Welcome to ListenLoop (the “Service”), a seven-day loop for English listening practice. By using the Service you agree to these terms; if you don’t, please stop using it.

sections.title: 1. What the Service is
paragraphs: The Service offers dictation, shadowing, and bilingual handouts, with built-in public-domain or Creative Commons material, ListenLoop’s official materials, and practices that users share publicly (shared materials). You can practice built-in and official materials without signing in; signing in syncs your progress across devices.
Some content (such as the English text, translations, vocabulary and grammar notes, and voices of official materials) is made by AI and may contain mistakes; treat it as a learning aid.

sections.title: 2. Accounts
paragraphs: You can sign in with Google, LINE, or an email and password; one email is one account whichever way you use. Keep your password safe and don’t reuse it on other sites; you’re responsible for activity on your account. If you’re under 18, use the service with the consent of a parent or guardian who has read these terms and the privacy policy; if you’re under 13, please don’t create an account.

sections.title: 3. Rules
paragraphs: When using the Service, don’t:
items: upload or share content that infringes copyright, trademarks, or other rights;
upload personal data, confidential information, or illegal, harassing, hateful, sexual, or violent content;
impersonate others, or access, disrupt, or attack the Service in bulk or by automated means;
get around the Service’s usage limits or security;
use the Service for anything illegal.

sections.title: 4. Content you upload
paragraphs: Text and recordings (the sound of an MP3 or MP4) you type or upload to make a practice stay yours or their rights holder’s. You must have the right to use them and are responsible for them.

To run the Service, you let ListenLoop store, process (including sending them to AI services for transcripts, translations, notes, and voices), and display them; when you make a practice public, you also let other users view, listen to, and practice it. You can make it private again or delete it at any time, after which we stop offering it.

A practice from a recording you upload starts private. Before making it public, you must confirm that you own the recording or have permission to share it (for example, you recorded it yourself, or the rights holder allows sharing); we record when you confirmed. Making someone else’s recording public without permission (such as a film, podcast, radio, or news program) may infringe copyright and is taken down under section 5.

sections.title: 5. Reports and takedowns
paragraphs: If you believe a public practice infringes your rights or is inappropriate, use “Report” on its page or tell us through “Feedback” at the bottom of the page, saying which practice and why.

We review every report and take the practice down when needed; its author sees the reason in My materials. An author who thinks a takedown is mistaken can explain through Feedback, and we’ll review it again. Accounts that break the rules repeatedly may be disabled.

sections.title: 6. Exam-style materials
paragraphs: Materials labeled “TOEFL-style,” “IELTS-style,” “TOEIC-style,” or “GEPT-style” imitate the format and difficulty only. Their content is original, not real test items, and the Service has no partnership with or license from the test makers.

sections.title: 7. Paid plan and subscriptions
paragraphs: Paid plans come in three lines: Listening, Writing, and All-in-One, each in Student, Plus, and Pro tiers; teachers have class plans (Small, Standard, and Large, in the same three lines). They are subscriptions billed monthly or yearly (a year costs ten months), at the prices and with the allowances on the Plans and pricing page. A Listening plan's writing is the free trial; a Writing plan's listening is the free plan's. Your own listening materials are counted in English words (reset monthly); the AI writing reviews and chats in essays, sets, and messages (reset weekly). A yearly plan's allowances still reset every month (writing every week) and don't carry over. Practicing official materials and the ones you've made is unlimited and uses no allowance. The student tier is verified by signing in with a school Google account and lasts a year; if it isn't renewed, the period already paid can be used to the end, but it won't renew at the student price. A third-party payment service handles payment.

Shared materials (practices other users share) can be practiced in full on Listening, All-in-One, and class plans; on the free plan, a Writing plan, or signed out, you can preview the first three sentences and listen to the first. You can always practice the materials you share yourself. A shared material you were already practicing when this rule began can be finished for that week.

Subscriptions renew automatically: at the end of each period, your payment method is charged for the next, until you cancel. Cancel any time on the Account page; you keep the paid plan until the period ends.

Refunds follow the refund policy: a full refund within 7 days of the first payment; a yearly plan ended early refunds its unused whole months. If prices change, we’ll announce it on the site and show it under "Plan and billing" on the account page before the next period starts, and you can cancel before the change applies.
When a subscription ends or you return to the free plan, your materials and progress are kept; you just can't add new materials.

sections.title: 8. Disclaimer
paragraphs: The Service is provided “as is.” We work to keep it running and its content accurate, but we don’t promise it will be uninterrupted or error-free, or any learning result or test score. Speech recognition depends on your browser and surroundings and is only a practice aid.
As far as the law allows, we aren’t liable for indirect losses from using or being unable to use the Service.

refund.intro: ListenLoop's paid plan is a digital service that renews automatically. This page explains how to cancel and when you can get a refund.

sections.title: 1. Cancelling renewal
paragraphs: Cancel any time under Plan and payments on the Account page. You won't be charged again; the paid plan lasts until the current period ends, then returns to Free.

sections.title: 2. Full refund within 7 days
paragraphs: Within 7 days of your first payment (monthly or yearly), you can ask for a full refund, no reason needed. The paid plan ends when it’s refunded.

sections.title: 3. Ending a yearly plan early
paragraphs: After 7 days, you can still end a yearly plan early: the unused whole months are refunded at that plan’s own monthly rate. For example, Plus All-in-One yearly at NT$2,690 used for 3 months and a few days refunds 8 × NT$2,690 ÷ 12 ≈ NT$1,793; Student Listening yearly at NT$900 refunds 8 × NT$900 ÷ 12 = NT$600 in the same case. The month already started isn’t refunded.
A yearly plan’s allowances still reset every month (writing every week); unused words, essays, sets, and messages don’t carry over or turn into refunds.

sections.title: 4. Later payments
paragraphs: Renewal payments generally aren't refunded. If you forgot to cancel and haven't created a material with the paid plan this period, ask within 7 days of the payment and we'll look at it.

sections.title: 5. How to ask
paragraphs: Use Feedback at the bottom of any page, with your account's email and the payment date. We reply within 5 working days. Refunds go back to the original payment method; how long they take depends on your bank or payment service.

sections.title: 6. Your materials after a downgrade

guide.title: For Beta testers
guide.intro: Thanks for helping test ListenLoop! Feel free to share this page with other testers.

sections.title: Signing up
items: Open the invite link we sent you (like listenloop-three.vercel.app/invite/XXXXXXXX). It works for 14 days.
Sign in with Google, and you're in (the quickest way). Email works too, but its confirmation message can take a while.
A phone with Chrome works best (Safari on iPhone is fine); shadowing needs the microphone. You can add it to your home screen like an app.

sections.title: What to do each day
items: Day 1: take the 2-minute level test, pick a recommended material, write down every sentence you hear, then read the notes and handout.
Days 2 to 6: shadow the same material each day.
Day 7: take the dictation again and see how far you've come since Day 1.
If you have time: pick a prompt under Writing and try its 7-day cycle (a first draft on Day 1, with AI feedback).
Each day unlocks on a new calendar day, so the 7 days can't be done at once.

sections.title: How long it takes
items: Listening takes about 10 to 15 minutes a day; writing about 15 (optional).
The test runs for 2 weeks; we may invite you to one or two 20-minute online interviews.

sections.title: Reporting a problem
items: Use Feedback at the bottom of every page, or Report a problem in the Account menu at the top right when signed in. Say what you did and what you saw; the page is attached for you.
A sentence's subtitle, translation, or sound is wrong: press Report a problem on that sentence.
Something is completely broken or urgent: message us directly.
"I didn't get this" and "I had to think here" are valuable feedback too.

sections.title: Privacy
items: We use practice records only to learn what works and where people get stuck. We never give your data to anyone or use it for ads.
Admin pages show an account number, not your email.
You're on the free plan during the test and are never charged.
You can delete your account on the Account page at any time, and all your data goes with it.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: How ListenLoop works, what's free, whether you need to sign in, and what shadowing needs: the questions people ask most. If yours isn't here, tell us.

what.question: What is ListenLoop?
what.answer: ListenLoop is an English listening practice site. You practice one 1–3 minute recording for seven days: dictation on Day 1, shadowing on Days 2–6, and dictation again on Day 7, compared with Day 1 so you can see your progress. The goal isn't the gist; it's hearing every word.

who.question: Who is it for?
who.answer: Anyone who wants solid listening skills: students preparing for the TOEIC, TOEFL, IELTS, GEPT, or the college entrance listening test, people about to study abroad, and professionals who need to follow meetings and calls in English. Materials come in beginner, intermediate, and advanced levels; the level test helps you choose.

free.question: Is it free?
free.answer: Official materials and the 7-day loop are free. The free plan can also make 300 words (about 2 minutes) of your own AI materials a week, with 2 AI essay reviews to try each week. Paid plans come in three lines (Listening, Writing, All-in-One) with more words of your own, uploading your own audio, playback speed, full practice of shared materials, more AI essay reviews and chats, and more. They're coming soon: join the waiting list; nothing is charged now.

signIn.question: Do I have to sign in?
signIn.answer: No. Without signing in, your progress is saved in this device's browser. Signed in (Google or email), your progress syncs to the cloud so you can continue on another phone or computer, and the home page shows today's tasks and your practice calendar.

loop.question: How does the 7-day loop work?
loop.answer: Day 1 is dictation: each sentence plays, you type what you hear, and every word is checked; the bilingual handout opens after you finish. Days 2–6 are shadowing: you repeat each sentence, and the browser's speech recognition marks the words you said and missed. On Day 7 you dictate the same recording again and compare it with Day 1, sentence by sentence.

unlock.question: Why can't I do all seven days at once?
unlock.answer: Each day opens after the previous one is done, on a later calendar day. Hearing the same recording again over several days is what links sounds to words; seven rounds in one day work less well. Days you've finished can be reviewed and practiced again any time.

pass.question: What if I don't pass on Day 7?
pass.answer: By default you pass when your Day 7 accuracy beats Day 1. If you don't, you practice the same material for another week; the earlier week's scores are kept for comparison. After passing, pick your next material. Paid plans can change the pass rules on the material's page, for example to a target accuracy.

retry.question: Can I redo a day? Does it change my score?
retry.answer: Yes, once that day's task is done you can practice it again. Your official score is your first completion; a retry only shows that round's score and never changes your results or whether you passed.

minutes.question: How long does it take each day?
minutes.answer: A material is 1–3 minutes of English: about 15 minutes on dictation days and about 10 on shadowing days. The library on the home page can filter by how many minutes you have today.

shadowing.question: What does shadowing need? What if I can't use a microphone?
shadowing.answer: Shadowing uses the browser's built-in speech recognition; Chrome on a computer or Android works best, with microphone access allowed. If the browser has no speech recognition, or the microphone is blocked or missing, you can still repeat each sentence and press "I said it" to mark it yourself.

materials.question: Where do the materials come from?
materials.answer: Official materials are original texts ListenLoop writes for learners, on daily life, travel, studying abroad, campus, work, news, exams, and more. They're read in American, British, Australian, and Indian accents, each with a Chinese translation, vocabulary, and grammar notes. A few are clips from CC BY-licensed open movies, always credited.

exams.question: Are there TOEIC, TOEFL, IELTS, or GEPT listening materials?
exams.answer: Yes, under Exam English: original listening practice in the style of the TOEFL, IELTS, TOEIC, GEPT (Elementary, Intermediate, High-Intermediate), Taiwan's senior high listening test, and the CAP, plus writing prompts for these exams and the GSAT, imitating their tasks and difficulty. Each exam has a guide with links to its free official practice. Apart from the marked official CAP items, they aren't real test items, and ListenLoop has no connection with any of these tests' organizers.

create.question: Can I make materials from my own text?
create.answer: Yes. Signed in, go to My materials and paste English or Chinese text (Chinese is translated first), choose a voice and accent, and AI makes the audio and handout. Allowances count English words: the free plan has 300 a week; Listening and All-in-One plans have 2,400 to 9,000 a month (by tier) and can also make materials from your own MP3 or MP4 recordings. Making one shows how many words it uses and how many are left this month. Materials can be private or shared publicly.

level.question: Which material should I start with?
level.answer: Take the level test: 2–3 minutes, no sign-in. You type a few sentences from easy to hard, and it suggests your level and a first material. Or pick a situation you like from Practice by topic.

devices.question: Can I switch between my phone and computer?
devices.answer: Yes. Signed in to the same account, your progress syncs with the cloud each time you open a page. Without signing in, progress stays in this browser only, and is lost if you change devices or clear your browsing data.

app.question: Is there an app?
app.answer: ListenLoop is a web app that works in any phone or computer browser. On your phone, choose "Add to Home Screen" in the browser to open it like an app.

delete.question: How do I delete my account and data?
delete.answer: Signed in, go to the Account page to download your data or delete your account. Deleting it removes your practice progress and history from the cloud, and cannot be undone. See the privacy policy for details.
